scope: Exploratory activation analysis on synthetic language prompts; not a complete interpretation or biological validation.

method.layer_selection: Validation ROC AUC, then validation effect size
method.null_layer_selection: Each null iteration independently selects its best validation layer before test evaluation

interpretation: The validation-selected direction generalized moderately to the separately formatted test prompts with ROC AUC 0.75. After repeating layer selection within every null iteration, the result exceeded the shuffled-label 95th percentile of 0.6875 (empirical p=0.0448) but equaled the random-direction 95th percentile of 0.75 (empirical p=0.0796). Residual, attention, and MLP interventions consistently shifted the selected output margin on four negative test prompts. The mixed null results and tiny authored test set are insufficient to identify a stable semantic feature or complete causal circuit.
limitations: All prompt sets were authored for this experiment and the final test set contains only eight prompts.
The format shift reduces but does not eliminate lexical, formatting, or dataset-construction confounds.
The empirical null results do not support a strong statistical claim for the selected direction.
Attention and MLP results operate on aggregate component outputs rather than individual heads or neurons.
Intervention sensitivity is not semantic proof or biological validation.
Results on Gemma 3 270M do not establish behavior of Gemma 4 31B or another checkpoint.
The bfloat16 results are not claimed to be numerically identical across hardware, drivers, or library versions.
No GMP, process-control, product-quality, clinical, or patient-safety conclusion is supported.
